title: Lead, Org Development and Culture
description:
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

When the game changes this fast, you need an expert to help teams adapt and perform at their best. We’re looking for an Organization Development Lead to drive organization development across our Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) geography. This role will support organization design, operating model activation, and transformation efforts that enable our strategy in a dynamic and diverse marketplace.

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

As an Organization Development Lead in EMEA your core responsibilities include:

  • Leading discrete initiatives or workstreams as part of local and global organization design, operating model, and transformation efforts to drive the highest impact and value in support of Nike’s strategic priorities
  • Partnering closely with business leaders and HR teammates to conduct organizational assessments, identify opportunities, and develop recommendations that improve organizational effectiveness, team performance, and ways of working.
  • Providing thought partnership on implementation and change enablement activities required to activate organizational and operating model changes successfully
  • Building capability in HR teammates and business leaders through coaching and formal learning experiences, equipping them with practical skills and tools to assess, lead, and sustain change
  • Consulting on broader HR and business initiatives through the lens of organization effectiveness, team effectiveness, and employee experience.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH

You will work with a broad set of stakeholders across a global matrix and diverse EMEA marketplace. Reporting to the Director, Organization Development EMEA, you will be part of the broader global Organization Development team and EMEA HR team. You will have opportunities to work on and lead projects across different parts of the EMEA Nike organization. To do your best work, you will collaborate with Organization Development teammates, senior business leaders, and partners across HR, Finance, Strategy, and Operations.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Experience designing and implementing cross-functional organization design, operating model, and transformation initiatives, leading key workstreams or deliverables
  • Proven experience delivering some or all of the following core capabilities: organization design, organization effectiveness, team effectiveness, capability assessment, and strategic alignment
  • Strong consulting skills including project scoping and management, proposal development, research and benchmarking, problem solving, and critical thinking
  • Skilled at creating clear, well-structured deliverables and presentation materials that simplify complex information, highlight key messages, and support decision making
  • Effective at designing and facilitating workshops that create engagement, alignment, and clear outcomes
  • Familiarity with leading practices in organization effectiveness and a passion for translating external insights and research into practical business solutions
  • Familiarity with change management practices and the ability to advise and partner with leaders on the successful activation and implementation of organizational change
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity, create clarity, and adapt plans to changing business needs. A high degree of adaptability, resilience, and flexibility to work across multiple projects and priorities is essential
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to engage confidently and effectively with a broad range of audiences, including senior leaders
  • NIKE’s business is conducted in English. Fluency in both written and spoken English is required for this role.

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace, and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

The Space & Airborne Systems (SAS) organization within Systems Engineering & Test Capabilities (SE&TC) is seeking a Systems Engineer II to join the Life Cycle Engineering (LCE) team. LCE Systems Engineers are responsible for supporting depot integration of hardware and software, developing test plans and procedures, debugging, and assessing system functions and interfaces, and verifying system requirements in preparation for final customer sell‑off.

The Life Cycle Engineering (LCE) department plays a critical role in back-end sustainment and repair design, sustainment development, and transitioning systems through integration and test as programs move from production into warranty and long-term support. To maintain program performance, meet contractual obligations, and ensure system readiness, additional Systems Integration & Test engineering support is required. Test event support activity may require travel, which is not expected to exceed 20%. This position is an onsite role in El Segundo, California.

What You Will Do:

  • Support Radar System Integration Laboratory (RSIL) and field/depot Integration, Verification & Validation (IV&V) activities, including troubleshooting hardware/software issues.
  • Perform system-level failure analyses using root‑cause and corrective‑action processes, advanced test equipment, and analytical techniques
  • Evaluate system performance and compile results using tools such as MATLAB, SQL, and other analytics platforms
  • Prepare and present clear technical reports and briefings for internal and external stakeholders, summarizing complex data into actionable insights.
  • Manage engineering support for hardware testing, troubleshooting, sustainment, and depot returns
  • Implement minor design updates informed by data trends, failure modes, and integration findings
  • Maintain and update engineering specifications and drawings
  • Coordinate technical discussions and tag‑ups across Program Management, Systems Engineering, and Chief Engineering teams.
  • Resolve system-level technical issues in collaboration with cross-functional engineering groups
  • Provide technical guidance to IPTLs and participate in team meetings, working groups, and interface discussions.
  • Support process implementation, mock‑up hardware repairs, and sustainment activities
  • Apply predictive analytics to anticipate failures, optimize maintenance, and improve lifecycle planning
  • Develop Python-based scripts/tools to analyze system/test data, automate workflows, and deliver actionable engineering insights

Qualifications You Must Have:

  • Typically requires a degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) discipline and a minimum of 2 years of prior relevant experience system engineering to include System Integration, Verification and Validation (IV&V)
  • Active and transferable U.S. government issued Secret security clearance is required prior to start date. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance

Qualifications We Prefer:

  • Airborne Radar Systems
  • Electrical test equipment, circuit, wiring, and electronic diagnostics tools: multimeters, oscilloscopes, tachometer, signal generator, etc.
  • Read and integrate software routines with hardware
  • Experience collecting and instrumenting large data sets, including using scripting or automation tools to support data acquisition and analysis.
  • Interpret and synthesize operational or test data to support system performance assessments and continuous improvement.
  • Microsoft Office, MATLAB, or Python, for data analysis and automation

What We Offer:

  • Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation
  • Relocation Eligible – Relocation assistance is available

title: Graduate Recruitment / Early Careers Consultant
description:
Your role

As part of our Early Careers team based in Melbourne, you'll help shape the future of the firm by attracting, engaging, and developing the next generation of talent. You'll work closely with partners, lawyers, and business teams to deliver market-leading recruitment and development experiences that identify high-performing students and support them to launch their careers at Allens.

This is a role for someone who enjoys taking ownership, building strong relationships and bringing ideas to life. You'll be trusted with meaningful responsibility from day one, supported by a collaborative team and encouraged to contribute new thinking as we continue to evolve our programs and candidate experience.

As an Early Careers Consultant you will:

  • Partner with stakeholders across the firm to attract, engage, select and onboard future talent.

  • Represent Allens as a brand ambassador, building relationships with universities and student communities through careers fairs, presentations and firm events.

  • Work closely with partners, lawyers and business teams to deliver engaging recruitment, development and networking opportunities for students.

  • Design and deliver market-leading engagement programs, including Dive In, helping high-performing students explore a career in commercial law.

  • Lead elements of our social media and attraction strategy, bringing creativity, curiosity and new ideas to how we engage emerging talent.

  • Design, project manage and deliver clerkship and graduate recruitment campaigns and development programs.

  • Identify and building relationships with emerging talent, providing exceptional candidate experience throughout the recruitment journey

  • Use data, insights, and technology to continuously improve our processes, programs and outcomes

This is a full-time maximum term contract for an initial period of 12 months to cover parental leave.

At Allens we have a hybrid working structure, typically 60% in the office and 40% from home. We would be happy to discuss any other flexible working arrangements that best support you.

About you

You will thrive in this role if you're someone who combines strong relationship-building skills with initiative, curiosity and a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes. You'll enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, balancing multiple priorities while maintain strong focus on stakeholder and candidate experience.

You will bring:

  • Experience in Early Careers recruitment, ideally within a law firm, professional services, or a similarly complex environment.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, including the ability to build credibility and influence senior stakeholders

  • Excellent collaboration skills and experience working across multiple teams and functions

  • Sound judgement, problem-solving skills and a willingness to take ownership and drive outcomes

  • Confidence using technology and data to work smarter and deliver better outcomes

  • A genuine passion for candidate experience and developing future talent

  • A desire and ability to grow as a recruitment and HR professional.

  • A desire to learn, grow, network, mentor others.

Your development

At Allens, we set a high bar for excellence and provide the support people need to grow. You'll have access to meaningful work, real responsibility and opportunities to build your capability through coaching, feedback and development experiences.

You'll be encouraged to take ownership of your career, explore new opportunities and continually develop your skills, judgement and confidence. Working alongside experienced colleagues and leaders, you'll be supported to expand your expertise and make a meaningful contribution from day one.

Our perks

Our benefits include:

  • Financial: market competitive fixed remuneration; salary continuance insurance, employee recruitment referral program, discounts at hundreds of suppliers including retail outlets, health and travel insurance, charity matched funding program.

  • Health and wellbeing: fully subsidised gym memberships, annual flu vaccinations, skin checks, in-house snacks and catered meals, subsidised sporting and social activities, emergency childcare, Employee Assistance Program including confidential counselling, wellbeing coaching and financial coaching for employees and their families and regular wellbeing sessions with our in-house consulting Psychologist.

  • Flexibility: hybrid and flexible working arrangements to support you in your work and life commitments and passions, equipment to support working from home.

  • Leave: ability to purchase additional annual leave, access to an enhanced, inclusive and flexible parental leave policy – 26 weeks paid parental leave with no minimum service for permanent employees and high quality executive coaching to support the transition.

  • Recognition: team based recognition including social activities and contribution based recognition activities, and annual Allens Values Awards to nominate and recognise the incredible contributions of our people.

Allens is also proud to invest in our communities, giving you the opportunity to make a difference through our work on reconciliation, the environment and other social justice issues as well as our workplace giving and volunteering programs.

How to apply?

We'd love to hear from you so please click "apply now"! If you would like to find out more, please visit 'This is Allens' or listen to our podcast 'Allens Confidential' to hear real stories from real people about life at Allens. Alternatively, for a confidential discussion, please get in touch with Meika Furlong, National Early Careers Manager at Meika.furlong@allens.com.au.

At Allens, our culture is made up of unique backgrounds and varying life experiences. We celebrate our people's differences across gender and gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, cultural backgrounds, First Nations communities, and family and caring arrangements. If you require adjustments to fully participate in our application process, please contact us at careers@allens.com.au.

We encourage applicants from all backgrounds, so if you're excited about this role but your past experience doesn't align, please express your interest by emailing us at careers@allens.com.au. The right role for you might be just around the corner!

title: Product Manager – Agentic Modernization
description:
Who We Are

At Kyndryl, we design, build, manage and modernize the mission-critical technology systems that the world depends on every day. So why work at Kyndryl? We are always moving forward – always pushing ourselves to go further in our efforts to build a more equitable, inclusive world for our employees, our customers and our communities.

The Role

Kyndryl is looking for a Lead Product Manager to own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle of Kyndryl's platform for Agentic Modernization — the platform that enables enterprises to modernize applications, processes, and operations through AI agents and agentic workflows. This role bridges customer needs, business objectives, and AI technology capabilities to deliver a secure, scalable, and enterprise-grade platform for building, deploying, governing, and operating AI agents at scale.

This is a senior, cross-functional leadership role. You will set the strategic direction for the platform, act as the primary liaison between the platform team and extended teams (solution engineering, client and account teams, partners, and delivery), and be accountable for the outcomes the platform enables across the modernization portfolio.

What You Will Do

  • Define and execute the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Kyndryl's Agentic Modernization platform.

  • Identify platform capabilities that accelerate the transformation of legacy business processes, applications, and workflows into AI-powered agentic experiences.

  • Gather and prioritize requirements from customers, developers, consultants, architects, delivery teams, and business stakeholders.

  • Collaborate with AI engineers, platform teams, UX designers, cloud architects, and modernization specialists to deliver platform capabilities and enhancements.

  • Own product backlogs, release planning, feature prioritization, and end-to-end lifecycle management.

  • Drive platform adoption by enabling the rapid creation, deployment, orchestration, monitoring, and governance of AI agents.

  • Establish and track success metrics, including modernization outcomes, platform adoption, agent deployment velocity, productivity gains, customer satisfaction, and business value realization.

  • Ensure enterprise-grade security, governance, compliance, and responsible AI practices are embedded throughout the platform lifecycle.

  • Serve as the primary liaison between the platform team and extended teams (solution engineering, client and account teams, partners, etc.), filtering and prioritizing incoming requests to the platform team.

  • Mentor and provide direction to junior product management resources supporting the platform.

Kyndryl currently does not require employees to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19, however, if you are hired to work at a client, customer, or partner location, you may be required to show proof of vaccination to align with their respective COVID-19 vaccination policies. Those who believe they are eligible may apply for a medical or religious accommodation prior to the start of employment.

Who You Are

Why Kyndryl:

We’re a purpose-driven company committed to innovation and empowering our people. Here, your work contributes to meaningful outcomes for clients and communities.

Your Future at Kyndryl

Every position at Kyndryl offers a way forward to grow your career. We have opportunities that you won’t find anywhere else, including hands-on experience, learning opportunities, and the chance to certify in all four major platforms. Whether you want to broaden your knowledge base or narrow your scope and specialize in a specific sector, you can find your opportunity here.

You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to provide it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in your work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others.

Kyndryl is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Kyndryl is also committed to compliance with all fair employment practices regarding citizenship and immigration status.

Required Technical and Professional Experience

  • Proven experience (typically 8+ years) in product management, with a track record of owning platform or product strategy end to end.

  • Demonstrated experience defining vision, strategy, and roadmaps for enterprise software or AI/platform products.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with experience acting as a liaison across engineering, delivery, client/account teams, and partners.

  • Experience prioritizing and balancing competing requirements across multiple stakeholder groups.

  • Strong grounding in AI/agentic technology concepts, including:

  • Agent orchestration, deployment, and governance

  • Responsible AI, security, and compliance practices

  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, including the ability to translate technical capabilities into business value.

  • Experience owning backlogs, release planning, and lifecycle management in an agile environment.

  • Understands the technology and the rapidly evolving AI market:

  • Knows what cloud providers, LLM providers, Broadcom, NVIDIA, and others are doing in the AI space

  • Can identify differentiated, scalable features the market needs

  • Can demonstrate the platform to cloud and LLM providers, internal executives, and clients

  • Can gather feedback, build and manage the roadmap, and work closely with Engineering to ensure delivery

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Experience with enterprise modernization initiatives spanning applications, cloud, mainframe, or network & edge domains.

  • Experience managing large, complex, multi-stakeholder platform programs at enterprise scale.

  • Background working with cross-functional AI, engineering, and consulting organizations.

  • Track record of driving platform adoption and measurable business outcomes.

Travel Requirements

This role requires a minimum of 25% travel to support client engagements, partner meetings, and cross-team collaboration across the modernization portfolio.

Diversity is a whole lot more than what we look like or where we come from, it’s how we think and who we are. We welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. That’s the Kyndryl Way.

With state-of-the-art resources and Fortune 100 clients, every day is an opportunity to innovate, build new capabilities, new relationships, new processes, and new value. title: Certified Inpatient Medical Coding Specialist (Remote)
description:
At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community. When we say every member of our community, that includes our employees. We know that when our employees feel cared for, heard and valued, they are inspired to create moments that exceed expectations, while prioritizing safety, compassion, personalization and efficiency. If you want to advance your career and contribute to our vision of creating healthier communities, now and for generations to come, we want you to be a part of our team.

Job Summary

POSITION IS REMOTE BUT YOU MUST MEET QUALIFICATIONS LISTED IN JOB DESCRIPTION.

**If you are located outside of the state of Texas -- you must be located in KANSAS, OKLAHOMA, TENNESSEE, LOUISIANA, GEORGIA, SOUTH CAROLINA, NORTH CAROLINA, or be willing to relocate to one of the eligible states (including Texas). **

Responsible for reviewing and abstracting inpatient medical records, as well as, identifying and assigning accurate medical codes for diagnosis, procedures and services in an inpatient setting. The Coding Specialist ensures that all data elements required for federal or state reporting and billing are collected and included in the patient’s demographic record. Typically reports to the Coding Manager.

Job Description

Job Description

Minimum Qualifications

Education: High School Diploma or GED required; Associates degree in Health Information Management or any Healthcare Related Field preferred

Licenses/Certifications: Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT), Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA), Certified Coding Associate (CCA), Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), or Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC) Coding Certification(s) from American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) or American Association of Professional Coders (AAPC) required.

Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

  • Three (3) years of inpatient hospital coding experience required.

  • Experience coding in a level 1 trauma facility/academic teaching facility strongly preferred.

  • Effective oral and written communication skills.

  • Strong knowledge of ICD-10-CM and PCS coding.

  • Analytical skills necessary to interpret data contained in the health records and to assign appropriate codes.

  • Proficient knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, medical terminology and surgical terminology.

  • Critical thinking, good judgment and decision-making skills.

  • Knowledge of coding compliance policies, official coding guidelines, regulatory requirements and internal policies and procedures affecting the coding process.

  • Proficient in navigating a Windows-based application environment.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Reviews medical record documentation to identify pertinent diagnosis/procedures that require code assignment for inpatient records and accurately code the diagnoses and procedures using ICD-10 coding conventions for the purpose of reimbursement, research, and compliance with federal regulations.

  • Reviews the medical record to assure specificity of diagnoses, procedures, and appropriate reimbursement for hospital and professional charges.

  • Queries physicians when code assignments are not straightforward or documentation in the record is inadequate, ambiguous, or unclear for coding purposes.

  • Keeps abreast of coding guidelines and reimbursement reporting guidelines and brings identified concerns to manager for resolution.

  • Effectively assigns DRG and ICD-10 codes to inpatient records.

  • Responsible in maintaining 92% to 95% in ICD-10 and DRG assignment and consistently meet established productivity standards while keeping abstracting errors to a minimum..

  • Abides by the Standards of Ethical Coding as set forth by the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) and adheres to official coding guidelines.

  • Ensures safe care to patients, staff and visitors; adheres to all Memorial Hermann policies, procedures, and standards within budgetary specifications including time management, supply management, productivity and quality of service.

  • Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency; supports department-based goals which contribute to the success of the organization; serves as preceptor, mentor and resource to less experienced staff.

  • Demonstrates commitment to caring for every member of our community by creating compassionate and personalized experiences. Models Memorial Hermann’s service standards by providing safe, caring, personalized and efficient experiences to patients and colleagues.

  • Other duties as assigned.
